---
title: "Research"
description: "Working papers, publications and data on decentralisation, urbanisation and local public goods in Africa, and on global value chains and regional development."
---

My research asks where authority and public money sit inside developing
countries, and what that placement does to economic outcomes. One strand
measures decentralisation and the provision of local public goods across
African cities. The other asks how foreign investment and global value chains
land in particular regions, and whether the green transition changes who
captures the value.

[**Primary fields:** urban and regional economics; political economy of
development; economic geography. **Secondary:** fiscal decentralisation and
local public finance; global value chains and foreign direct investment;
computational measurement of institutions.]{.fields}

Drafts not linked below are available on request.

## Featured paper

::: {.pubs}
- **Status without Power: The Political Economy of Administrative Unit Creation in Uganda**
  [Single-authored]{.authors}
  [Submitted to the CSAE Conference 2027]{.venue}
  [Uganda has repeatedly carved new administrative units out of old ones, often for political reasons. This paper treats that politically selected, block adoption of new units as a quasi-experiment and uses a staggered difference-in-differences design with spatial structure to measure what the new units actually do once they exist.]{.desc}
  [[Request draft](mailto:o.harman@lse.ac.uk?subject=Status%20without%20Power)]{.links}
:::

## Working papers

::: {.pubs}
- **Measuring Metropolitan Authority in Africa: A Regional Authority Index for Eight Countries, 1994–2024**
  [Harman, O., Hayward, J., and Sampó, G.]{.authors}
  [IGC Working Paper, in preparation]{.venue}
  [Extends the Hooghe–Marks Regional Authority Index to the metropolitan tier, where Africa has had almost no coverage. National constitutional and statutory instruments are coded with large language models and validated against in-country experts and legislative sources.]{.desc}

- **Green Foreign Direct Investment in Africa**
  [Alvarez-Vilanova, J., Crescenzi, R., Harman, O., and Lippitsch, C.]{.authors}
  [In preparation]{.venue}
  [Asks whether green investment in Africa builds industrial capability in the places that host it, or moves the value elsewhere.]{.desc}

- **Transforming SME Integration into Global Value Chains**
  [Harman, O., Shukla, R., and Nasir, R.]{.authors}
  [In preparation]{.venue}

- **Degree of Urbanisation in Ethiopia**
  [Franklin, S., Harman, O., Kakoulaki, G., Molla, K., and Read, M.]{.authors}
  [In preparation]{.venue}
:::

## Publications

### Articles

::: {.pubs}
- **Unequal Progress and Barriers for Women in Economics**
  [Berland, O., Harman, O., and Moreau-Kastler, N.]{.authors}
  [In press, *Reviews of Economic Literature*, Stanford University Press. Earlier version: "Pipelines or pyramids: A review of barriers for women in economics", IGC Working Paper (2023)]{.venue}
  [Reviews recent evidence on the barriers women face in economics. Gender gaps have narrowed over the past decade, but unevenly across institutions and countries and mostly at senior levels, and the evidence points to differences in evaluation standards, lower recognition of women's contributions and signs of a hostile environment.]{.desc}
  [[Working paper (SSRN)](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4879332) [IGC version](https://www.theigc.org/publications/pipelines-or-pyramids-review-barriers-women-economics)]{.links}
:::

## Doctoral thesis

::: {.pubs}
- **Power and Place: Decentralisation, Urbanisation and Local Economic Development in Africa**
  [DPhil in Sustainable Urban Development, University of Oxford, in progress. Supervised by Vlad Mykhnenko]{.venue}
  [Asks how decentralisation is changing across Africa and what follows for local economic development. The thesis builds a framework of capacity, authority and means, applies it to eight countries across three decades, and studies the creation of new administrative units in Uganda as a quasi-experiment.]{.desc}
:::

## Data

::: {.pubs}
- **RAI(Metro) Africa**
  [A Regional Authority Index at the metropolitan tier for eight African countries, 1994–2024, coded from national legislation against the Hooghe–Marks codebook and validated with in-country experts. Open release of the data and coding pipeline in preparation]{.venue}

- **CAM Africa Database**
  [Capacity, authority and means indicators for sub-national governments across eight African countries. Citable deposit in preparation]{.venue}

- **Mapping Municipal Finance Reform in Developing Countries**
  [Interactive data visualisation, International Growth Centre]{.venue}
  [[View](https://www.theigc.org/media-items/mapping-municipal-finance-reform-developing-countries)]{.links}
:::
